title: Whole organ and organism tissue clearing by uDISCO
protocol: Anesthetize the animals deeply with MMF.
Transcardially perfuse the animals with heparinized 0.1 M PBS.
Perfuse the animals with 4% paraformaldehyde in 0.1 M PBS.
Remove the skin and carefully open the skull and vertebra without damaging the CNS tissue.
Store the mouse body in 0.1M PBS at 4°C up to 4 weeks if not clearing immediately.
Collect tissues directly and post-fix them in 4% PFA for 1-2 days at 4°C.
Wash the samples once in 0.1M PBS for 5 min before clearing.
Prepare _tert_-butanol solutions with distilled water at various volumes (30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, and 100%).
Use Dichloromethane as a pure solution for the delipidation step.
Mix BABB and diphenyl ether at a ratio of 4:1 (Vol/Vol) to prepare BABB-D4 solution.
Add 0.4% Vol vitamin E into BABB-D4 solution.
Mix BABB and diphenyl ether at a ratio of 10:1 (Vol/Vol) to prepare BABB-D10 solution.
Add 0.4% Vol vitamin E into BABB-D10 solution.
Mix BABB and diphenyl ether at a ratio of 15:1 (Vol/Vol) to prepare BABB-D15 solution.
Add 0.4% Vol vitamin E into BABB-D15 solution.
Incubate fixed samples in 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, and 100% tert-butanol for 2-12 hours at 34-35°C.
Incubate samples in DCM for 45-60 minutes at room temperature (skip this step for small tissues like mouse spinal cord or 1 mm-thick coronal slices).
Incubate samples in BABB-D solution until they become optically transparent.
Establish the transcardial-circulatory system as in Figure 1.
Connect the Viton reference tubing to the peristaltic pump.
Insert the tubing connectors at each end of the Viton tubing.
Connect the tubing connectors with additional PVC tubing for extension.
Cut the head part of the 1 ml syringe as a connector and insert it into the outflow tubing of the pumping channel.
Connect the transcardiac perfusion needle for mouse or the thinnest perfusion needle without rubber head for rat with this connector.
Fix the inflow tubing of the recirculating channel in the glass chamber containing animal body ready for clearing.
Keep a certain height between the inflow tubing head and bottom of the glass chamber to ensure that the sample is covered by clearing solutions during clearing at all times.
Keep the inflow tubing of the pumping channel beneath the surface of the clearing solution.
Start the circulation until air bubbles are pushed out from the tubing system.
Set the perfusion needle into the heart of the animal through the same pinhole made during perfusion.
Circulate the clearing solutions one by one as indicated in Table 1.
Use a heating plate at 35-40 °C for 100% tert-butanol circulation steps to prevent the solution from solidification.
Set the flowing rate at 8-10 ml/min for mouse clearing and 15-20 ml/min for rat clearing.
Circulate BABB-D10 until full transparency is achieved (about 6-12 hours for mouse and ~24 hours for rat).
